subject: Subcommittee Restructuring and Open Meeting Law
overview: The Medford Energy and Environment Committee voted unanimously to disband its formal subcommittees to comply with Open Meeting Law while continuing informal working groups below quorum thresholds. Members also reviewed preparations for upcoming public events and received updates on regional clean energy and transportation plans.

items.title: Call to Order, Member Status, and Minutes
items.summary: Committee member Dave Hampton announced his resignation due to moving out of town, and the committee approved the May 2, 2022 meeting minutes.

items.title: Administrative Updates and City Budget
items.summary: Staff introduced four summer interns, reported on the upcoming municipal budget hearings, and discussed the status of a letter sent to the mayor regarding gas-powered leaf blowers.

items.title: Harvest Your Energy Festival
items.summary: The committee discussed planning for the October 15 Harvest Your Energy Festival, including vendor logistics and potential recognition of the net-zero Medford Public Library.

items.title: Open Meeting Law and Subcommittee Disbandment
items.summary: The committee voted unanimously to disband all formal subcommittees to remain compliant with state Open Meeting Law, opting to handle preliminary work through informal, non-quorum working groups.

items.title: Circle the Square Preparations
items.summary: Members coordinated logistical details, staffing shifts, and educational display materials for their table at the upcoming Circle the Square community event.

items.title: Energy, Reforestation, and Regional Transit Updates
items.summary: The committee discussed National Grid's renewable gas proposals, Massachusetts heat pump rebate programs, state reforestation legislation, and the MBTA's proposed bus network redesign.
